description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge): 3 surveys, 2 real blasts and 2 phantom ones, and 5 contract acceptances against a mine that goes formally bankrupt before the first blast ever fires -- named for a $250k win, but `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (locked) and, under #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling, the $150,000 budget can no longer fund the 12-person roster staffed:true adds through even the first drilling wait. BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized. fires at tick 132, 205 ticks before blast 1 and long before the operator (per this file's own command sequence) notices or stops; see the pattern-1 drill-wait step and Findings #59-#60 for the full trajectory. Interaction-mode finding, this file's own: once levelEndReason turns non-null at tick 132, LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay (z-index 9999, every panel/toolbar control sits at z 100-200) covers the whole screen for the rest of the run and never clears -- no player click reaches ANY panel again after that tick, including blast 1's own charge/sequence/execute and every contract-accept/drill-plan-grid step that follows. Every step past tick 132 that mutates state now runs its command directly (role:'guard' + expect.blocked, same convention this file already used for its phantom blasts) instead of pretending a click still lands. #593 (GameLoop.ts's autoInsertNeedTasks no longer preempting an employee's own interrupted work the instant their rest completes, and VehicleReservation.ts's releaseVehicleReservation now syncing a dismounting driver's real position) changes the trajectory this file records: pattern 1 lands only 23 of its 24 holes before blast 1 fires (2 deaths, not 4, since one driller/rig pair is still short of its hole), which leaves one drill_rig alive to fully drill pattern 2 (25/25) for a second real blast (3 more deaths, 5 total) before patterns 3 and 4 revert to genuinely phantom (both rigs destroyed by blast 2, never replaced). Final balance: -$1,282,536 (#591: updated from -$1,271,073 -- staffed-fleet spawn spacing and vehicle occupancy reroute shift exact pathing/payroll timing without changing the trajectory in kind).

issue #585: the repo-wide commandOutcome audit found this file's 4 contract-deliver steps refused with 'Not enough <ore> in storage: 0.0 kg available' no matter how many ticks preceded them. Direct trace (createGameEngine + runCommand replay) found the real cause: this file never once builds a freight_warehouse anywhere in its 187 steps -- and HaulingTask.ts's requestHaulFragment (the only code path that ever increments storedMassKg/collectedOre, called from both the manual haul and the auto-dispatch haul_debris action alike) hard-requires findNearestActiveBuildingOfType(..., 'freight_warehouse', ...) to resolve a depot before a hauler will so much as pick up a fragment. With none built, storedMassKg traced flat at 0.0 for 600+ ticks past blast 1 regardless of wait length -- not a timing gap, a missing prerequisite. Fixed by building one here instead of the second rock_digger this file also bought: sandbox-traced across the full 187-step file, vehicle #5 (that purchase; staffed's own #3 already covers rock_digger and sits idle the whole run too) never got a driver or left 'idle' -- this file drills no ramps (no dig_ramp_segment command anywhere in it), the only task type a rock_digger claims, so the purchase was dead weight both before and after this fix. Swapping it for a $15,000 T1 warehouse ($35,000 cheaper than the rock_digger it replaces) at (2,8) -- clear of all 4 drill patterns' footprints (confirmed via trace: patterns span roughly x10-37/z15-46) and close to the vehicle spawn row (z:2) -- actually improves the cash trajectory (was $3,278 after all 3 buys, now $38,278) rather than worsening it, and (also confirmed via trace) leaves blast 1's own death toll and timing untouched, unlike every warehouse tile tried closer to the drill patterns, which perturbed blast 1's own navgrid-dependent hole-completion timing and its death count. Interaction is a real build-panel click (this step lands at tick 32, well before the tick-132 bankruptcy overlay that blocks every later click in this file) -- a command-only interaction here would have let command mode and interaction mode silently diverge on world state from this point on, exactly what .claude/rules/scenario-defs.md warns against. The vehicle-buy-assign step right after this one now assigns driller #8 to vehicle #6 (drill_rig), not #7 -- see that step's own note.

Was an unmarked command step that overdrew: the Fleet panel disables a dealership row on `cash < def.purchaseCost` (setTierButtonAffordable, FleetPanel.ts), so no click could buy this while the console bought it anyway. The console now refuses an unaffordable purchase and the run is funded for the fleet, so this is a real click on the debris_hauler tier-1 row ($25,000). awaitUsable is the affordability assertion. issue #585: re-opens the Fleet panel explicitly -- the previous step now builds a freight_warehouse (Build panel) instead of buying a second rock_digger (Fleet panel), so Fleet is no longer already open here the way it was before.

After hiring, surveying and the 3-vehicle fleet, cash sits at $3,278 -- already under BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000, balance.ts) before a single tick of this wait runs. BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100) later, 'BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized.' fires at tick 132 (state.bankruptcy.bankrupt / state.levelEnded flip to true, state.levelEndReason to 'bankruptcy', Bankruptcy.ts) -- inside this very first tick chunk, 205 ticks before the 2 driller/drill_rig pairs actually finish sinking this 24-hole pattern (tick 337) and long before blast 1 ever fires. Nothing in the engine stops a `tick` command from continuing to run a level after levelEnded flips (a genuinely pending EVENT, like the Explosive Tariff below, is the only thing that ever halts one), so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working -- for the rest of this file.

#553: resolves the Explosive Tariff event that cut this tick call short at tick 140 (108 of 150 requested) -- politics_explosive_tariff option 0 pays the $20,000 tariff in full (fixed, RNG-free delta). CI finding, this PR (#586): was role:player driving `resolveEventIfPending`'s real click -- state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 132 (8 ticks before this event pends), and the event dialog's own overlay class (`.bs-confirm-overlay`, EventModal.ts) sits at z-index 600, far below `--bsx-z-menu` (9999) that LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay has owned since tick 132 -- same class of bug as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps further down this file, just on a dialog instead of a panel, and reached earlier because this event happens to pend this late. Every other 'event choose 0' step in this drilling wait stays role:player safely because `resolveEventIfPending` no-ops (no click at all) when nothing is genuinely pending; this is the one step in the wait where an event really is pending at the moment it runs, so it is the one that actually reaches `resolveEventIfPending`'s bare `page.click('#bs-event-dialog .bs-event-choice')` -- which has no `describeUnclickable` wrapper, so Puppeteer's own unnamed 'Node is either not clickable or not an Element' surfaced instead of a diagnosis. Converted to guard + expect.blocked, command run directly so cash still drops by the tariff. Update: EventModal now also defers behind LevelEndScreen once the level has ended (UIManager.update, matching BlastReportModal's own fix for the same z-index gap) -- its .bs-event-choice buttons are never rendered at all in that state rather than rendered-but-covered, so probing for them reports 'absent', which expect.blocked itself rejects as unprovable (scenario-goal.ts/interaction-driver.ts). Reassigned to #bs-event-dialog, the dialog's own outer overlay -- created once in EventModal's constructor and left in the DOM at display:none, so it is the one still-present, genuinely-hidden control left to assert against.

issue #585 (originally command-mode-only): switched from `type:ore_sale` to `type:rubble_disposal`. Direct trace at this exact tick (after the freight_warehouse fix and the raised wait above) found blast 1's own drilled footprint yields only rustite ore (collectedOre: {rustite: ~425}, confirmed via trace) -- none of blingite/absurdium/sparkium/dirtite, the ore-sale materials this run's own seed happens to be offering at this point, will ever be deliverable here no matter the wait.
